facts.value: Until the 18th century, Sharia law was practiced throughout the Muslim world in a non-codified form.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: The Ottoman Empire's Mecelle code in the 19th century was the first attempt at codifying elements of Sharia law.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: Since the mid-1940s, efforts have been made in country after country to bring Sharia law more in line with modern conditions and conceptions.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: In modern times, the legal systems of many Muslim countries draw upon both civil and common law traditions as well as Islamic law and custom.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: The constitutions of certain Muslim states, such as Egypt and Afghanistan, recognize Islam as the state religion and obligate the legislature to adhere to Sharia.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: Saudi Arabia recognizes the Quran as its constitution and is governed based on Islamic law.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: Iran has also witnessed a reiteration of Islamic law into its legal system after 1979.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: One of the fundamental features of the movement of Islamic resurgence has been the call to restore the Sharia.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: The call to restore the Sharia has generated a vast amount of literature.
facts.programme_association: Law, Human Rights in Criminal Justice - LLM or MA

facts.value: The restoration of Sharia has affected world politics.
